blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in `users`) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
findings.recommendation: The proposal promises that the button "erases the member's personal data" and that orders are kept "without personal data", but `delete_account` only soft-deletes: `email`, `display_name`, `phone` and `postal_address` (app/schema.sql:3-6) stay in the `users` row, which `orders.user_id` still references, so the orders remain linked to an identified person. Scenario: member 1 (ada@example.org, Ada) clicks "Delete my account"; afterwards `SELECT email, display_name, phone, postal_address FROM users WHERE id = 1` still returns all four — the right to erasure (GDPR Art. 17) and storage limitation (Art. 5(1)(e)) are not met. Because `email` is UNIQUE, the kept address also blocks the person from signing up again. Overwrite or NULL these columns in the same UPDATE (e.g. email replaced by a non-identifying placeholder such as `deleted-<id>@invalid`, display_name by a neutral value, phone and postal_address NULL), keeping only the id the orders need, and add a test asserting the row no longer holds any of them.
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in `users`

findings.recommendation: The salted hash is pseudonymous, not anonymous: anyone holding `ANALYTICS_SALT` can recompute it from the kept user id, so analytics events carrying it stay personal data after deletion. `delete_account` neither purges nor detaches those events, and the change does not say where they are stored or for how long. Confirm with the team where analytics events live and either delete the member's events on account deletion or state why the pseudonymous id is acceptable; the analytics store was not visible in this repository.
findings.title: Erasure does not reach analytics events keyed by `analytics_id`

findings.evidence: - A "Delete my account" button erases the member's personal data and signs them out everywhere; their orders are kept for accounting, without personal data.
findings.recommendation: Neither the plan nor the code says how long backups of `members.db` keep a deleted member's data or how a restore avoids bringing it back. Ask the team to state the backup retention period and the rule for re-applying deletions after a restore; nothing about backups was visible in the repository.
findings.title: Retention and erasure in backups are not defined
